:::{#exm-anderson-exp-mle}
#### Exponential rate estimates for the leukemia trial

By the [MLE of the exponential rate parameter](intro-to-survival-analysis.qmd#thm-mle-exp),
each group's estimated hazard rate is its number of relapses
divided by its total follow-up time:

```{r}
#| label: anderson-exp-mle
anderson |>
  summarize(
    .by = rx,
    relapses = sum(status == "relapse"),
    follow_up = sum(survt),
    rate = relapses / follow_up
  )
```

For the new treatment, 9 relapses over 359 weeks of follow-up give
$\ehaz_{\text{new}} = 9/359 \approx 0.0251$ relapses per week;
for the standard treatment, 21 relapses over 182 weeks give
$\ehaz_{\text{standard}} = 21/182 \approx 0.1154$.
The estimated log hazard ratio is then:

$$
\ba
\logf{\frac{\ehaz_{\text{standard}}}{\ehaz_{\text{new}}}}
&= \logf{\frac{21/182}{9/359}}
&& \text{(substitute the rate estimates)} \\
&= \logf{\frac{21 \cdot 359}{182 \cdot 9}}
&& \text{(divide fractions)} \\
&= \logf{\frac{7539}{1638}}
&& \text{(multiply)} \\
&\approx 1.527
&& \text{(evaluate)}
\ea
$$

The `survreg()` fit's `rxstandard` coefficient, $-1.527$,
is the negative of this log hazard ratio, as the exponential AFT model predicts,
and its intercept, $3.686$, is $\logf{359/9}$,
the log of the estimated mean remission time on the new treatment.

:::
